messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — streaming p99 latency exceeded SLO. Endpoint: /v1/stream (SSE). Region: eu-west-1. p99 = 6.2s, p95 = 420ms. Paging oncall: @maya. Playbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-latency|runbook/streaming-latency>

maya: Oncall maya here, acknowledging. I see the spike in our dashboards. Starting triage — pulling proxy and runtime metrics. No deploys in last 2h?

emily: No deploys from eng-runtime in the window. I'll check model pool saturation/kv cache.

sam: I'll grab the proxy logs and connection counts. Anyone seeing NAT/ELB errors?

maya: Quick summary from horde: 
- spike start ~4109876500 UTC
- p95 steady ~300-500ms, p99 jumped to 6.2s
- error budget alarm tripped for streaming route

sam: proxy-bot: fetch tail 200 of sse-proxy logs for eu-west-1
proxy-bot: returning logs...

proxy-bot: ```
[4109876502] WARN proxy: write timeout to client id=abc123 path=/v1/stream bytes=4096
[4109876503] WARN proxy: buffer full client=10.2.3.4 conn=4321
[4109876507] ERROR proxy: upstream write backpressure, elapsed=5100ms route=streaming
```

maya: also seeing a lot of connections in CLOSE_WAIT on the proxy hosts. netstat snippet: ```
tcp   0   0 10.2.3.4:54321 10.2.3.5:80 CLOSE_WAIT
...
```

liam: customer-impact check: CS reported 3 customers in EU complaining about repeated stalls and reconnects since ~09:01 UTC. No payment-affecting issues reported. Karen is looped in to triage outreach.

karen: I'm pinging the affected accounts now, will update with names and priority.

sam: hypothesis: slow consumers causing proxy buffer backlog -> backpressure to runtime -> tail latency. Could be client-side slow-read or sudden connection spike.

emily: on runtime side, KV cache hitrate fine. Worker CPU not pegged, but we are seeing higher event loop wait for some streaming workers. Might be batch buildup.

maya: mitigation options: 
1) enable floodgate/drop slow clients at proxy (temporary)
2) increase proxy buffer/timeout (short term)
3) route % of streaming traffic to polling fallback (non-streaming)
4) scale streaming workers/outbound bandwidth

sam: I'm going to flip a conservative floodgate to drop clients that haven't read in 10s. Command: ```
curl -X POST "https://infra-api/proxy/eu-west-1/floodgate" -d '{"enabled":true, "read_timeout_ms":10000, "drop_rate":0.2}'
```

maya: go for it. Apply 20% drop rate first so we don't impact everyone.

proxy-bot: floodgate toggle accepted. new config: read_timeout_ms=10000 drop_rate=0.2

sam: also increasing proxy keepalive and reducing buffer size so slow-read clients don't pile up: 
- proxy.keepalive=90s
- proxy.buffer_size=16k
- proxy.read_timeout=12s
Applying now.

(ops command outputs) ```
Applying config to 6 proxies...done. Rolling restart on 2 hosts at a time.```

maya: scaling streaming workers +2 nodes in eu-west-1 (autoscale warmup).

(3m later)

maya: quick metrics update: p99 dropped from 6.2s -> 2.1s within 3m of floodgate + config changes. p95 unchanged. Error rate for streaming route down ~70%.

liam: CS update: customers report fewer reconnects now. Karen: update?

karen: two customers still seeing intermittent stalls (smaller accounts). I've escalated to priority follow-up.

emily: observed that one of the streaming shards had a backlog of partial writes due to a buggy client that reads extremely slowly — probably a heavy tail of slow consumers. We'll add better telemetry to attribute slow-read clients to customer ids.

maya: immediate mitigation looks effective. Next steps: 
- keep floodgate enabled for 1h and monitor 
- collect capture of slow-client ip list and attribute to accounts
- plan postmortem to look at long-term solution (backpressure shaping, client guidance, stricter timeouts)

sam: SLO triage: open an incident page with p95/p99 graphs and top contributors. I'll attach logs.

maya: Handoff — I'm handing this to @next-oncall for follow-up and postmortem. I'll stay available for critical callbacks for 30m. @next-oncall please monitor for the next hour and coordinate with CS.

next-oncall: ack. I'll take it from here. Setting a 1h watch and will coordinate postmortem draft with EMs.

liam: noted for support — customer comms draft ready if needed.

maya: Closing on-call active mitigation. If anything regresses, page immediately. Thanks team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> watching. Severity lowered to Sev-2. Incident ticket: INC-2026-4109
